description: Alaska-only rules checked against the cited statutes and official DMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Unless a different limit is posted, Alaska's maximum in a residential district is
questions.explanation: 13 AAC 02.275(b)(3) sets 25 miles per hour in a residential district unless otherwise posted. The Alaska DOT&PF travel page quotes the same regulation.

questions.q: Unless a different limit is posted, the maximum in an Alaska business district is
questions.explanation: 13 AAC 02.275(b)(2) sets 20 miles per hour in a business district unless otherwise posted. Alaska DOT&PF lists the same figure.

questions.q: Unless a different limit is posted, Alaska's maximum in an alley is
questions.explanation: 13 AAC 02.275(b)(1) sets 15 miles per hour in an alley unless otherwise posted.

questions.q: Alaska's basic speed rule in 13 AAC 02.275(a) requires a driver to
options: Drive the posted maximum in any weather
Not exceed a reasonable and prudent speed for conditions
Use 55 mph whenever no sign is visible, even in an alley
questions.explanation: 13 AAC 02.275(a) says no person may drive at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent considering the traffic, roadway, and weather conditions. The numbered maximums apply except when a special hazard requires a lower speed.

questions.q: Alaska's driving-under-the-influence chemical-test standard for a motor vehicle is
options: 0.10 percent or more in the blood
questions.explanation: AS 28.35.030(a)(2) uses a chemical test taken within four hours showing 0.08 percent or more by weight of alcohol in the blood, 80 milligrams or more per 100 milliliters of blood, or 0.08 grams or more of alcohol per 210 liters of breath.

questions.q: A person at least 14 and not yet 21 commits Alaska's minor-operating offense by driving
options: After having consumed any quantity of alcohol
Only if a passenger is also a minor
questions.explanation: AS 28.35.280(a) applies when that person operates or drives a motor vehicle, or operates an aircraft or watercraft, after having consumed any quantity of alcohol. Subsection (b) says any alcohol concentration in the blood or breath is a basis to cite the person.

questions.q: Operating a commercial motor vehicle in Alaska is a crime under AS 28.33.030 when a test within four hours shows
options: 0.04 percent or more, in blood or breath
Any alcohol only if the driver is under 21
questions.explanation: AS 28.33.030(a)(2) sets that 0.04 commercial standard. The section also covers driving a commercial motor vehicle under the influence, or under the combined influence of an alcoholic beverage, an inhalant, and a controlled substance. 0.04 percent or more by weight of alcohol in the blood, or 0.04 grams or more per 210 liters of breath.

questions.q: Alaska law requires suspension, revocation, or denial of a license when points reach
questions.explanation: AS 28.15.221(b) requires the point system to suspend, revoke, or deny for 12 or more points from offenses during any consecutive 12-month period or 18 or more points from offenses during any 24-month period. The Alaska DMV points page states the same mandatory thresholds.

questions.q: If an Alaska licensee is convicted of two or more traffic violations from a single occasion, points are assessed for
options: The offense with the greater point value only
No points if one charge is speeding
questions.explanation: AS 28.15.231(c) says points are assessed for one offense only, and if the point values differ the assessment is for the offense with the greater point value.

questions.q: An Alaska noncommercial instruction permit may be issued to a person who is at least
questions.explanation: AS 28.15.051(a) allows a person who is at least 14 to apply. The permittee must be accompanied by a person at least 21 who has been licensed at least one year for that type or class of vehicle, who can exercise control, and who occupies a seat beside the driver.

questions.q: An Alaska provisional license at ages 16 and 17 requires proof of at least
questions.explanation: AS 28.15.055(2) requires a parent, legal guardian, or employer to prove at least 40 hours, including at least 10 hours in progressively challenging circumstances such as inclement weather and nighttime driving. The applicant must also have held an instruction permit at least six months and have no traffic-law conviction in the six months before applying.

questions.q: A person driving on an Alaska provisional license may not drive between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless
options: The trip is inside the city
For work, or with an adult 21+
questions.explanation: AS 28.15.057(b)(2) states those exceptions. Passenger limits in the same subsection allow a parent, legal guardian, sibling, or a person at least 21, or require that at least one passenger be a parent, legal guardian, or person at least 21. The person is accompanied by a parent, legal guardian, or licensed person at least 21, or is driving to or from work or within the scope of employment by the most direct available route.

questions.q: Alaska will not issue an ordinary driver's license to a person who is at least 16 but not yet 18 unless that person has
options: Held a provisional license for at least six months
Completed 50 hours after the provisional license
Held only an instruction permit for 30 days
questions.explanation: AS 28.15.057(a) also requires an instruction permit for at least six months and no traffic-law conviction during the six months before the application. The provisional-license restrictions themselves do not apply to restricted licenses issued for areas off the connected road system while the person is operating in those areas.

questions.q: In Alaska, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Alaska issues a learner's permit for a car at 14 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Alaska car permit: 14 years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: INSTRUCTION PERMIT, Division of Motor Vehicles, State of Alaska

questions.q: In Alaska, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Alaska requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

provenance.manual: Provisional License, Division of Motor Vehicles, State of Alaska

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Alaska complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Alaska requires 40 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: In Alaska, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Alaska, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Alaska not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Alaska restricts provisional drivers from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Alaska new drivers: off the road 1 a.m. to 5 a.m..

provenance.manual: Provisional License, Division of Motor Vehicles, State of Alaska

questions.q: In Alaska, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Alaska drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 16½ years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Alaska car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Alaska car knowledge test has 20 questions.

provenance.manual: Reinstate Your Driving Privileges - Alaska DMV

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Alaska car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Alaska car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Reinstate Your Driving Privileges - Alaska DMV

questions.q: In Alaska, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Alaska, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Alaska, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

provenance.manual: DUI (DRIVING UNDER THE INFLUENCE) COURT REVOCATION, Division of Motor Vehicles, State of Alaska

questions.q: In Alaska, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Alaska sets the under-21 limit at 0.00%.

provenance.manual: UNDERAGE DRINKING - ZERO TOLERANCE, Division of Motor Vehicles, State of Alaska

questions.q: In Alaska, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Alaska brings a suspension of 90 days.
questions.remember: Alaska, first refusal: 90 days without a license.

provenance.manual: DUI (DRIVING UNDER THE INFLUENCE) COURT REVOCATION, Division of Motor Vehicles, State of Alaska

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Alaska?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Alaska can be posted up to 65 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Alaska rural interstate: up to 65 mph.

provenance.manual: Transportation & Public Facilities - State of Alaska

questions.q: Which best describes Alaska's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
questions.explanation: Alaska: only texting is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Alaska?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Alaska, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: from a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Alaska left on red: onto a one-way street only.

provenance.manual: Credential Services, Division of Motor Vehicles, State of Alaska

questions.q: How is Alaska's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Alaska seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Alaska?
questions.explanation: Alaska requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Alaska: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: What is Alaska's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Alaska requires at least $50,000 / $100,000 / $25,000.

provenance.manual: Mandatory Insurance, Division of Motor Vehicles, State of Alaska

questions.q: Under Alaska's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Alaska can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 12 months.

provenance.manual: POINTS, Division of Motor Vehicles, State of Alaska
